## Research 1/4: what exists today

All paths and lines are at `origin/main` 1613e42f9. This research ran no build and no test (research lane).

### Two stock engines, two jobs
| Engine | Code | Job today |
|---|---|---|
| Column (dexel height field) | `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/dexel.rs` lines 10-33 (`Dexel`: one material top per XY column, tiled storage); cut in `cut.rs` `simulate` line 138; cell from `auto_cell` (`cut.rs` lines 35-40: `min_radius / 8`, at most 1023 cells on an axis; `kernel.rs` line 20: `MAX_CELLS_PER_AXIS = 4096`) | **The verdict.** `crates/app/src/stock_sim.rs` `simulate_document` (line 141) gives rest, gouge and deviation. The post gate reads it. `backend.rs` lines 32-36: "The column arm is what ships." |
| Field (sparse brick SDF, the "voxel" stock) | `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/field.rs` lines 37-43 and 81-120 (`SdfField`: 8x8x8 bricks of f64 in a `HashMap`, a mesh layer, a cut layer, two ray-entry layers); cut in `field_cut.rs` lines 18-42 (cut = running max of the negated swept-tool distance); batch and cost law in `field_batch.rs` lines 12-30 and 43-59 | **The display.** `crates/app/src/stock_view.rs` lines 9-13: "A display field, not a verdict." Playback is `crates/app/src/stock_play.rs` lines 1-31. Retirement of the column engine is #26 (M7.3). |

### How a move is cut on the field (CPU)
- The tool solid is exact, not voxelized. A ball sweep is a capsule (closed form). Other tools are a 1-D convex minimum along the move, by golden section with 32 iterations (`field_sweep.rs` lines 14-23, sweep kinds lines 27-43: lathe, ball, shanked, revolve (flat, taper, drill, bull), true XY arc).
- The sign of the mesh layer is ray parity against the shell, live (`field.rs` lines 17-24 and 164-178). The cut layer can only lift the distance. Thus a cell is air only where a tool reached it.
- A move whose window spans more than `MAX_CELLS_PER_MOVE = 1 << 22` cells refuses by name (`field_cut.rs` line 77).

### The display path today
1. Precalculation before playback (#2181): `crates/sim/src/play_precalc.rs` cuts the program stride by stride and keeps keyframes (clones of the cut stock). Lines 8-9: "Display only ... the verdict and the post gate never read it."
2. Pack: the sparse f64 bricks become a dense f32 lattice (`stock_sim/preview/pack.rs` lines 1-23). The budget is `MAX_TEXELS = 1 << 23` texels (32 MB) for each layer.
3. Upload: the first frame sends the mesh layer and the cut layer. A later playback frame sends only the dirty bricks as texel runs (`preview/patch.rs` lines 1-17; `crates/ui/src/trace.rs` lines 229 and 236-243 `write_cut_patch`; `trace/eye.rs` line 262).
4. Draw: `crates/ui/src/trace.wgsl` (219 lines) sphere-traces the dense lattice in a compute pass (Hart 1996). Bindings: `mesh`, `cut`, `tgt` read-only, `out` per pixel (lines 24-31). The CPU twin is `trace/cpu_eye.rs`. The parity suite is `crates/ui/tests/trace_parity.rs`.
5. Refusal: a device that refuses the kernel, or a lattice past the storage limit, gives `Err`, and the CPU march runs at thumbnail size (`trace.rs` lines 19-22; `trace/eye.rs` lines 9-13, `GPU_PIXELS` line 53, `CPU_PIXELS` line 56).

The GPU only draws. All removal is on the CPU.

### Cost drivers today
- **The display cell is coarse on purpose.** `stock_view.rs` lines 33-39: `DEFAULT_TEXELS = MAX_TEXELS / 32` (262 144 texels). The comment says that finer cells "cost the field subtraction cubically (the flat tool's spanning flank sweeps the whole stock height per move)". The cell is `cbrt(stock volume / texels)` (`stock_view.rs` lines 220-221). Example: a 200 x 150 x 60 mm block gives a cell of about 1.9 mm.
- Each cell in the window of each move runs the distance law (golden section for non-ball tools).
- Each keyframe is a clone of the cut layers (`play_precalc.rs`, `play_keys.rs`).
- The pack converts the sparse bricks to dense f32 on the CPU, then the upload copies it.

### A fact for #2611 (not worked here)
At a 1.9 mm display cell, a cut that is shallower than about one cell can show little or no change on screen. This research does not say that this is the cause of #2611. The worker of #2611 can check it.

### Existing windowless GPU and parity pattern
- `crates/ui/src/headless_gpu.rs` lines 1-6: software adapter first (lavapipe, WARP), then hardware. Line 37: `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU` turns the loud SKIP into a failure (#615).
- #2620 moves this policy into a new crate `camcraft-gpu`.

## Research 2/4: the open questions (grid, removal, read-back)

Sources are published literature and public specifications only:
- Van Hook, "Real-time shaded NC milling display", SIGGRAPH 1986 (dexel).
- Tukora and Szalay, "Multi-dexel based material removal simulation and cutting force prediction with the use of GPGPU", Adv. Eng. Softw. 43(1), 2012, 65-70.
- Tarbutton, Kurfess, Tucker, Konobrytskyi, "Gouge-free voxel-based machining for parallel processors", IJAMT 69, 2013, 1941-1953.
- Inui, Umezu, Shinozuka, "A Comparison of Two Methods for Geometric Milling Simulation Accelerated by GPU", Trans. ISCIE 26(3), 2013.
- Schnös, Hartmann, Obst, Glashagen, "GPU accelerated voxel-based machining simulation", IJAMT 115, 2021, 275-289.
- Museth, "VDB", ACM TOG 2013. Hoetzlein, "GVDB", HPG 2016. Crassin et al., "GigaVoxels", I3D 2009.
- The W3C WebGPU and WGSL specifications, and the wgpu 30 documentation.

### Q1. Grid design and resolution
Memory for one f32 layer of a 200 x 150 x 60 mm block:

| Layout | Cell | Size |
|---|---|---|
| Dense | 1.9 mm (today) | 1 MB |
| Dense | 0.5 mm | 58 MB (fits the 128 MiB default `maxStorageBufferBindingSize`) |
| Dense | 0.25 mm | 460 MB (does not fit) |
| Sparse band, 8 cells deep | 0.25 mm | about 52 MB, x2-3 with the machined surface |
| Dexel, Z only | 0.1 mm | about 24 MB for each interval; tri-dexel x3 |

**Recommended:**
- Slices 1-3 use a dense lattice in the `preview/pack.rs` layout. `trace.wgsl` reads this layout today. `pack_cut` is the bit reference. The budget stays `MAX_TEXELS`.
- A later slice adds a sparse brick pool with a page table (GVDB, GigaVoxels). The CPU makes the brick work list from the move windows. The GPU fills the cells.
- The display cell follows the pixel size, not the setup tolerance. The verdict stays on the CPU in f64, at its own resolution.

**Dropped:**
- A GPU dexel or tri-dexel stock. It needs a new renderer and a new CPU reference. #26 moves the verdict to the field, not to dexels. Inui et al. also say that a Z-map does not show overhangs.
- An octree. A pointer walk is slow on a GPU, and a two-level brick pool gives the same memory gain.

### Q2. Material removal on the GPU
- One invocation for each cell, for each batch of moves. The batch is the `field_batch.rs` batch (`BATCH_MOVES = 1024`).
- The cut is `max(cut, -d_tool)` (`field_cut.rs` lines 18-42). The max commutes. Thus `atomicMax` on an order-preserving f32-to-u32 map gives the same bits in each run, in any order. WGSL has atomics on `i32` and `u32` only.
- WGSL has no f64. The kernel uses coordinates relative to the tile, to keep f32 error small.
- The f32 tool distance is made conservative. The GPU never removes more than the CPU f64 law. This keeps the "conservative direction" law of `field_cut.rs`.
- The first kinds: ball and upright flat end mills on linear moves. Arcs (the true circle), bull, taper, drill, shanked tools and posed 4- and 5-axis moves come in a later slice. A kind that has no kernel refuses by name, and the CPU cuts it. A rapid touches nothing, as on the CPU.

### Q3. Read-back and verdicts
**Recommended: no verdict reads a GPU value.** Rest, gouge, deviation and collision stay on the CPU. Today that is the column engine. After M7.3 (#26) it is the field engine.
- Read-back is for the parity tests only (`map_async`). For 32 MB it takes some ms. This research did not measure it.
- An optional GPU reduction can give a status number for the display. It is labelled as display only.

**Dropped: a GPU verdict filter for removal now.** Reasons:
- It needs a superset parity test and fault injection, as #2622 has for the gouge pairs.
- `field_batch.rs` already skips cells with exact proofs (lines 12-30).
- Revisit it after #26, with a measurement.

The gouge pair filter stays in #2622. This issue does not duplicate it.

## Research 3/4: display, backends, determinism, relation to other work

### Q4. Display integration
**Recommended:**
- The removal kernel writes the `Scene.cut` storage buffer of `crates/ui/src/trace.rs` directly. The CPU pack and the dirty-brick patch upload (`trace.rs` lines 229 and 236-243) are then not necessary on the GPU path.
- Keyframes are GPU buffer copies, within a VRAM budget. A seek copies the nearest keyframe and dispatches the remaining moves.
- Generation runs outside the frame, as the precalc rule says (#2238, frame target under 10 ms). A frame only draws.

**Dropped:** a field of "removal move index" for each cell. A prefix of the program then needs a compare for each cell, but the value is not exact for a cell that two moves cut. Keyframes plus a dispatch give the exact prefix.

### Q5. Backends, wasm, timeout
- Native: Vulkan, Metal and DX12 through wgpu 30 (today through `egui-wgpu =0.36.2`).
- Browser: WebGPU has compute. The display needs no read-back, thus the browser needs no blocking wait. WebGL2 has no compute (`DownlevelFlags::COMPUTE_SHADERS`), so WebGL2 uses the CPU path. #2623 owns the browser probe.
- Timeout guard:
  1. Limit the size of each dispatch so that it stays far below the Windows TDR (default 2 s).
  2. On `DeviceLost`, or on any error, the CPU path runs. Log this one time.
  3. `CAMCRAFT_GPU_COMPUTE=off` (#2620) turns the GPU path off.
- #2424 (a Radeon freeze) is a reason for a small dispatch size and the off switch.

### Q6. Determinism and tests with no GPU
- On one adapter, the max law with atomics gives the same bits in each run.
- Across adapters, the result agrees within a stated tolerance. The parity is one-sided: GPU cut <= CPU cut + margin, and GPU cut >= CPU cut - k * eps.
- Tests run on the software adapter (`headless_gpu.rs`). With no adapter, a test does a loud SKIP. `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1` makes the SKIP a failure (#615).
- The CPU twin is the reference. The CLI, MCP and the runners with no GPU use the CPU path. Their results do not change.
- **Prime Directive:** no GPU value goes into a verdict, the post gate or the posted G-code. The CPU f64 judgement has the final word.

### Q7. Relation to other work
- `camcraft-sim` keeps the verdict. The GPU path is display playback only.
- Rest material for Adaptive and Pocket stays on the CPU.
- M7.3 (#26, #586, #637, #589) does not change. It is independent: it changes the verdict engine, and this work changes the display path. A later change to the `field_cut.rs` laws must also change the WGSL kernel. Use named twin constants and a parity test, as `trace.wgsl` and `cpu_eye.rs` do.
- simview (#2586, #2587, #2592) uses the GPU playback through `camcraft-gpu`. #2268 (move `FieldPlay` to sim) helps this, but it does not block slice 1.
- **The GPU display work waits for #2611.** A playback that shows no removal is a broken CPU reference. A parity test against it has no value. Slice 1 (the CPU twin) does not wait.
- The GPU display work also waits for #2620 (the device home).

## Research 4/4: one home, the decision, and the slices

### One home for GPU compute code: `camcraft-gpu` (#2620)
**Chosen:** all GPU compute kernels of this work go into the `camcraft-gpu` crate that #2620 makes. The device policy, the probe and the CPU fallback are there already in the #2620 plan.

Why:
- simview (#2586, #2587) must not depend on `camcraft-ui` or flecs. A kernel in `camcraft-ui` is not available to simview.
- The CLI and the tests need the windowless device. #2620 gives it.
- One home agrees with the coordinator note on #2620.

How:
- A kernel takes the device and queue that the caller gives. The viewport gives the egui device. Thus the cut buffer binds to the trace with no copy. The types are the same because the wgpu version is pinned.
- A later slice moves `trace.rs` and `trace.wgsl` into `camcraft-gpu`, so that simview can draw.
- The `camcraft-gpu -> camcraft-sim` edge needs a `docs/decisions/` entry (AGENTS.md "No new dependency between our crates without a decision"). The imported items are more than five: the sweep and tool data, the lattice meta, `CutPatch`, and the pack functions.
- #2525 put its evaluator in `camcraft-ui`. #2615 follows this home too. The #2620 coordinator note already says so.

**Dropped:**
- Kernels in `camcraft-ui`: simview and the CLI cannot use them.
- Kernels in `camcraft-sim`: this puts wgpu into the verdict crate. #2622 keeps sim free of GPU code, and this work does the same.

### Decision
**Build in part.** The GPU does the display playback cut. It does not do a verdict. The CPU f64 engines keep the final word.

### Slice order
1. S1: the CPU f32 twin of the cell kernel, and the brick work list. Headless, no GPU, testable now.
2. S2: the GPU removal kernel (ball and flat, linear moves). Blocked by S1 and #2620.
3. S3: the viewport playback on the GPU. Blocked by S2 and #2611.
4. S4: the other tool kinds and moves. Blocked by S2.
5. S5: a sparse GPU brick pool for a finer display cell. Blocked by S3.
6. S6: simview and browser WebGPU use the GPU playback. Blocked by S3 and #2587.

### Not answered by this research
- Measured speeds. Research runs no build and no benchmark. S2 and S5 measure.
- The cause of #2611. This research did not work it.
- The exact wgpu 30 API for a poll with a timeout. The S3 worker checks it.

The sub-issue numbers follow in the closing comment.

Research complete. The answers are in the four comments above. The decision: build in part. The GPU does the display playback cut. The CPU f64 engines keep each verdict. The home for GPU compute code is `camcraft-gpu` (#2620).
